A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Puzzle research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Appendices A and B match after accounting for page and table renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark, throughput, human-evaluation, long-context, alignment, and ablation results, including detailed RULER results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds GKD-budget experiments, randomized architecture comparisons, and compression baselines.

M1.justification: The main BLD–MIP–GKD procedure, search space, and losses remain unchanged. Section 7.1 newly describes limited derivative adaptations: miniPuzzle, attributed to Blakeman et al., enforces homogeneous blocks, while the 405B derivative subsequently incorporates FFN Fusion and continued pretraining.

E1.justification: Section 7.1 newly includes MMLU-Pro alongside existing benchmarks in aggregate derivative evaluations. The training corpora, human-evaluation tasks, and detailed RULER coverage are retained. The new budget and randomized-architecture studies otherwise reuse existing tasks.

E2.justification: v5 adds Random-from-block-library, Fully Random, and Parent-Randomized comparisons in Table 15, plus Wanda and low-rank approximation in Table 17. Section 8.4 also reports Wanda after distillation. Minitron, ShortGPT, and SlimGPT are discussed but are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New designs include reduced GKD budgets, a 10B-token randomized-architecture comparison with speed constraints for the architecture variants, and compression comparisons specifying 2:4 Wanda sparsity and distilled low-rank layers. Section 7.1 adds larger/hybrid parent configurations and deployment constraints. Existing throughput settings are clarified rather than demonstrably changed.

E4.justification: v5 adds GKD-budget sensitivity results addressing how much uptraining is necessary and randomized controls testing architecture selection beyond access to trained blocks. It also reports the effect of distillation after Wanda pruning. The earlier BLD, scoring, search-space, greedy-search, and long-context analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The human evaluation retains 169 samples and three independent annotators per sample. New randomized baselines do not introduce reporting of repetitions or statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: New results include 99.63% accuracy preservation for Nemotron-49B at 8.68B GKD tokens, MMLU 79.7 versus 66.02 for Puzzle and Random-from-block-library at 10B tokens, and Wanda/low-rank comparisons. Section 7.1 also adds derivative-level results. Existing main and appendix scores remain; these additions do not establish improved performance under the earlier settings.

T1.justification: The search-space definitions, channel-contribution derivation, MIP objective and constraints, diversity constraint, and distillation-loss equations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the 2.17× throughput and 98.4% accuracy-preservation headline from Nemotron-51B to both 51B and 49B. The introduction adds a roughly 4B-token efficiency claim and promotes 49B into the contribution list. The central hardware-aware NAS claim remains, and 49B long-context/alignment capabilities were already reported in v4.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges that 45B-token uptraining may exceed practical budgets and argues that users can reduce GKD accordingly. Section 8.4 adds an interpretation of pruning and low-rank methods as complementary block-library options. The conclusion removes proposed investigations of distribution shifts, task adaptation, and alternative search algorithms.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly discloses automatic TP/batch-size selection, including TP1/batch 256 for Nemotron-51B and TP4/batch 384 for its parent. Table 3 identifies nonoptimal TP1 entries as equal-resource comparisons. Section 7.1 adds deployment specifications and model-access information for Nemotron-Ultra.

R1.justification: New Section 8.4 substantially expands positioning through direct compression comparisons and the claim that Minitron, ShortGPT, and SlimGPT occupy restricted subsets of Puzzle’s optimization space. References to Wanda, factorized-layer initialization, SlimGPT, FFN Fusion, and Nemotron-H are added; earlier citations remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution list receive localized revisions, additional evaluations are grouped under Section 7.1, and new comparison subsections are inserted. The conclusion is shortened and acquires a duplicated retrieval-augmented-generation fragment. Most exposition and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds three compact tables for GKD budgets, randomized architectures, and compression comparisons. Table 3 gains explanatory markers and a footnote; Figure 5 and other floats move with text reflow. The eight existing figures and appendix table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new budget studies, randomized controls, compression comparisons, and throughput disclosures modestly strengthen empirical support and practical interpretability. Reporting errors limit the gain: Section 8.2.4 calls a parent-relative percentage Nemotron-relative, and Table 17’s low-rank scores imply 76.485 rather than its reported 76.05 average. The abstract also extends the efficiency headline to 49B without matching supporting tables. These issues weaken quantitative precision, although the component scores still support the added baseline rankings.
